question: What is the main purpose of the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: To measure the vehicle's top speed capability
choice_b: To test knowledge of hazardous materials regulations
choice_c: To evaluate a driver's paperwork and logbook accuracy
choice_d: To test for the basic skills needed for safe control and operation of the vehicle
explanation: The manual states the Basic Control Skills test tests for the basic skills needed for safe control and operation of the vehicle, since these skills are also required in many different driving situations.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: Before entering or exiting the vehicle to check around it during a backing exercise, what must you do first?
choice_a: Sound the horn twice and wait for the examiner's signal
choice_b: Remove your seatbelt and open all windows
choice_c: Turn off the headlights and radio
choice_d: Set the parking brake and place the vehicle in neutral
explanation: The manual requires that when entering/exiting the vehicle you must set your parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is scored as a "pull-up" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Backing up during a forward-moving exercise
choice_b: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_c: Crossing over a boundary line with the vehicle's mirror
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
explanation: A pull-up is defined as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position, and the examiner scores the number of times this happens.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: Which two exercises specifically score pull-ups?
choice_a: Only Exercise 1 - Forward Stop
choice_b: Only the on-road Road Test
choice_c: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
explanation: The manual states pull-ups are scored on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: According to the manual, will you be penalized for your initial pull-ups?
choice_a: Yes, but only during Exercise 1
choice_b: Yes, every single pull-up results in automatic failure
choice_c: No, pull-ups are never scored under any circumstance
choice_d: No, but an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: A "back-up" is scored on which exercise?
choice_a: Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_c: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing
choice_d: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop
explanation: A back-up is backing up during a forward-moving exercise, and "back-ups" are scored on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many free back-ups are allowed on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Two free back-ups
choice_b: One free back-up
choice_c: There are no free back-ups allowed
choice_d: Unlimited back-ups
explanation: The manual states there are NO free back-ups on this exercise, and you are not permitted to exit the vehicle during it.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: What is scored as an "encroachment" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors
choice_b: Sounding the horn too early at the end of an exercise
choice_c: Braking too gently while approaching a stop box
choice_d: Shifting gears more than twice during an exercise
explanation: An encroachment is crossing over or touching exercise boundary lines or cones with any portion of the vehicle other than the mirrors or other unique vehicle parts at or above door mirror height.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What must you do if you encroach on a boundary during an exercise?
choice_a: Stop immediately when signaled by the examiner and return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries
choice_b: Exit the vehicle and request a different exercise route
choice_c: Restart the entire Basic Control Skills test from the beginning
choice_d: Continue the exercise and ignore the encroachment
explanation: If you have encroached, the examiner will stop you and you must return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries, stopping immediately when signaled.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: What is scored as a "look" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Checking the side mirrors while remaining seated
choice_b: Using a turn signal before backing
choice_c: Sounding the horn at the end of the exercise
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle, opening the door, or moving from a seated position to check the vehicle's position while backing
explanation: A look occurs when you open the door, move from a seated position, or exit the vehicle to check its external position while performing a backing exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: How many free looks are allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing versus Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Unlimited free looks on both exercises
choice_b: One free look on Exercise 2 and two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_c: Zero free looks on either exercise
choice_d: Two free looks on Exercise 2 and one free look on Exercise 4
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

question: On a bus, what action counts as a "look" during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Honking the horn once
choice_b: Turning on the interior dome lights
choice_c: Walking to the back of the bus to get a better view
choice_d: Adjusting the driver's seat position
explanation: The manual specifically states that on a bus, if you walk to the back of the bus to get a better view, it will count as a look.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills Scoring - Final Position
question: Final vehicle position is scored on which two exercises?
choice_a: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: All four exercises equally
choice_c: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: Only during the on-road Road Test
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Basic Control Skills Scoring - Final Position
question: What happens if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner?
choice_a: You receive a warning with no penalty
choice_b: You will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
choice_c: The exercise is skipped without being scored
choice_d: You are automatically given three additional attempts
explanation: The manual warns that failing to maneuver into the final position as instructed results in penalty and failure of the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions and Unsafe Acts
question: What may happen if you fail to follow the examiner's instructions for completing an exercise as directed?
choice_a: A minor point deduction with no other consequence
choice_b: An automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner
choice_c: The examiner will complete the exercise for you
choice_d: A retest is automatically scheduled for the same day
explanation: Failure to follow examiner instructions for completing the exercise as directed may result in automatic failure and test termination.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions and Unsafe Acts
question: Which of the following is given as an example of an "unsafe act" that may result in automatic failure?
choice_a: Asking the examiner for clarification of instructions
choice_b: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion
choice_c: Driving slightly under the posted speed limit
choice_d: Using a turn signal earlier than necessary
explanation: The manual gives forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion as examples of an unsafe act that may cause automatic failure.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.1 Scoring

topic: Failure to Follow Instructions and Unsafe Acts
question: If you see the examiner raise their hand during an exercise, what should you do?
choice_a: Sound the horn and accelerate forward
choice_b: Continue the exercise exactly as planned
choice_c: Stop and return your vehicle within the exercise boundary lines
choice_d: Immediately exit the vehicle
explanation: The manual instructs that if you see the examiner raise their hand, you must stop and return your vehicle within the exercise boundary lines.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, Introduction

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, where must the front most part of your vehicle come to rest?
choice_a: Within the box at the end of the alley, without going past it
choice_b: Anywhere within three feet of the box
choice_c: Exactly on the far boundary line of the box
choice_d: Past the box by no more than one foot
explanation: The exercise requires driving forward through the alley and stopping with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: How many times may you stop during Exercise 1 - Forward Stop?
choice_a: Three times
choice_b: Only once
choice_c: As many times as needed
choice_d: Twice
explanation: The manual states plainly, "You may stop only once" for this exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: After stopping in Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, what must you do to signal completion to the examiner?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn
choice_b: Turn on the hazard lights only
choice_c: Rev the engine three times
choice_d: Exit the vehicle and wave to the examiner
explanation: The manual instructs that when stopped, you set your parking brake, shift to neutral and sound the horn, which informs the examiner to score the exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how far must you back through the alley?
choice_a: Until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley
choice_b: Exactly 50 feet, regardless of cone position
choice_c: Until the rear of the vehicle touches the alley wall
choice_d: Until the parking brake engages automatically
explanation: You back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
choice_a: Three free pull-ups and unlimited exits
choice_b: One free pull-up and one exit to check around the vehicle
choice_c: Zero free pull-ups and no exits allowed
choice_d: Two free pull-ups and two exits
explanation: The manual allows one free pull-up and permits exiting the vehicle only one time to check around it during this exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: During Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, you will be scored on which factors?
choice_a: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_b: Number of gear shifts only
choice_c: Speed and fuel usage only
choice_d: Turn signal usage only
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position on this exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What does Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking demonstrate?
choice_a: Your ability to parallel park at a curb
choice_b: Your ability to reverse in a straight line
choice_c: Your ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward
choice_d: Your ability to make a U-turn in a narrow alley
explanation: The manual describes this exercise as demonstrating the ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, where should the right most rear tire be kept while steering into the opposite lane?
choice_a: Directly on top of the cone
choice_b: At least five feet from the cone
choice_c: Between the cone and the line
choice_d: Directly on the center line
explanation: You drive forward and steer left through the opening into the opposite lane, keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: Are you permitted to exit the vehicle during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Yes, one time only
choice_b: Yes, an unlimited number of times
choice_c: Yes, up to two times
choice_d: No, you are not permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise
explanation: The manual explicitly states there are no free back-ups and you are NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, within what distance must the rear most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within three (3) feet
choice_b: Within one (1) foot
choice_c: Within six (6) inches
choice_d: Within ten (10) feet
explanation: You must bring the rear most part of your vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley in this exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: Four free pull-ups and unlimited exits
choice_c: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_d: Zero free pull-ups and no exits
explanation: The manual allows two free pull-ups and permits exiting the vehicle a maximum of two times during this exercise.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must be true about the vehicle's position within the alley when Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing is complete?
choice_a: The vehicle must be facing forward rather than backward
choice_b: The vehicle must be angled at approximately 45 degrees
choice_c: The vehicle must be straight within the alley and completely within the defined exercise boundaries
choice_d: The vehicle may extend beyond the outer boundary line if needed
explanation: The manual requires the vehicle be straight within the alley and completely within the defined exercise boundaries, and it may not go beyond the outer boundary line.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following must you do at all times?
choice_a: Wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_b: Keep the radio on for the examiner's convenience
choice_c: Maintain the maximum posted speed at all times
choice_d: Keep one hand off the wheel to demonstrate control
explanation: The manual requires that at all times during the test you must wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: If your test route does not include a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing, what may the examiner ask you to do?
choice_a: Automatically fail that section of the test
choice_b: Skip that entire portion of the scoring with no discussion
choice_c: Simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_d: Drive to a different area specifically to find the situation
explanation: The manual states that if the route lacks a certain traffic situation, you may be asked to simulate it by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: Before approaching a turn, what should you do to warn others of your intent?
choice_a: Sound the horn continuously
choice_b: Roll down the window and signal by hand only
choice_c: Flash your headlights repeatedly
choice_d: Use turn signals
explanation: As you approach the turn, the manual instructs you to use turn signals to warn others of your turn.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: What is defined as "unsafe coasting" in the turns section?
choice_a: Braking too early before reaching a turn
choice_b: When your vehicle is out of gear for more than the length of your vehicle
choice_c: Coasting downhill in neutral for less than one car length
choice_d: Driving more than 5 mph over the posted speed limit
explanation: Unsafe coasting occurs when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: After completing a turn, what should you do regarding your turn signal and lane position?
choice_a: Make sure the turn signal is off, get up to the speed of traffic, and move into the right-most lane when safe
choice_b: Immediately move into the left-most lane
choice_c: Turn off your headlights
choice_d: Leave the turn signal on until your next turn
explanation: After the turn, you must make sure the turn signal is off, get up to speed of traffic, use a turn signal, and move into the right-most lane when safe.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As you approach an intersection where you must stop, what is required?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop, with no coasting, behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines
choice_b: Stop only if another vehicle is directly ahead of you
choice_c: Accelerate through before checking traffic in all directions
choice_d: Slow down but keep rolling through if no traffic is visible
explanation: If necessary, you must come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what must you avoid doing?
choice_a: Keeping your hands on the wheel
choice_b: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Decelerating and yielding to pedestrians
choice_d: Checking your mirrors
explanation: The manual instructs that you must not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While stopped at an intersection, what must your vehicle not do?
choice_a: Have its headlights illuminated
choice_b: Have the parking brake engaged
choice_c: Roll forward or backward
choice_d: Idle for more than 10 seconds
explanation: The manual states, "Your vehicle must not roll forward or backward" while stopped at an intersection.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, where should your vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Straddling two lanes for better visibility
choice_b: In the left-most lane at all times
choice_c: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with traffic flow without exceeding the speed limit
choice_d: On the shoulder of the road
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: Before changing lanes during the on-road test, what must you do first?
choice_a: Slow down to half the posted speed limit
choice_b: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals before changing lanes
choice_c: Turn on your hazard flashers
choice_d: Signal and change lanes immediately without checking traffic
explanation: The manual instructs you to make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Before entering the expressway, what should you do?
choice_a: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane
choice_b: Shift into neutral to coast onto the ramp
choice_c: Turn off your headlights while merging
choice_d: Come to a complete stop at the on-ramp before merging
explanation: Before entering the expressway, you must check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the exit ramp of an expressway, what must you continue to do?
choice_a: Change lanes immediately upon entering the exit ramp
choice_b: Come to a full stop and check mirrors before proceeding
choice_c: Continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between vehicles
choice_d: Accelerate to merge back into the main flow of traffic
explanation: Once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: For the Stop/Start maneuver, where must you move your vehicle before stopping?
choice_a: Into the center turn lane
choice_b: To the right-most lane or shoulder of the road
choice_c: To the left-most lane
choice_d: Onto the sidewalk
explanation: You must check traffic thoroughly in all directions and move to the right-most lane or shoulder of the road for this maneuver.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Once stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, what should you activate along with the parking brake?
choice_a: Your headlights only
choice_b: Your four-way emergency flashers
choice_c: The interior dome light
choice_d: The horn
explanation: Once stopped, you must cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and move the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from a Stop/Start maneuver, what should you check and do before the vehicle moves?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel fully before releasing the parking brake
choice_b: Check traffic and mirrors, turn off the four-way flashers, activate the left turn signal, and do not turn the wheel before the vehicle moves
choice_c: Immediately release the parking brake and accelerate hard
choice_d: Shift directly into the highest available gear
explanation: The manual instructs you to check traffic and mirrors, turn off the four-way flashers, activate the left turn signal, release the parking brake when traffic permits, and not turn the wheel before the vehicle moves.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve, when should you reduce speed?
choice_a: Before entering the curve, so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Speed should never be reduced for a curve
choice_c: Only if another vehicle signals you to slow down
choice_d: Only after you have entered the curve
explanation: The manual instructs that before entering the curve, you should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: Before reaching a railroad crossing, what should all commercial drivers do?
choice_a: Change lanes to get a better view of the tracks
choice_b: Always come to a full stop regardless of signals
choice_c: Decelerate, brake smoothly, shift gears as necessary, and look and listen for trains
choice_d: Accelerate to clear the crossing as quickly as possible
explanation: Before reaching the crossing, all commercial drivers should decelerate, brake smoothly, shift gears as necessary, look and listen for trains, and check traffic in all directions.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: While any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what must the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Keep both hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Continue looking for approaching trains
choice_c: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
choice_d: Maintain a steady speed across the tracks
explanation: The manual states you must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For drivers of buses, school buses, or placarded vehicles, within what distance range should the vehicle stop from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 10 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_b: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Exactly 100 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Within 25 feet but not less than 20 feet
explanation: The manual specifies that these drivers should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail at every railroad crossing (unless exempt).
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For buses, school buses, and placarded vehicles, when should the four-way flashers be deactivated at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Immediately upon seeing the railroad crossing sign
choice_b: After the vehicle crosses the tracks
choice_c: Before reaching the crossing
choice_d: They should remain on for the rest of the route
explanation: The manual states that four-way flashers should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_a: The color of the overpass structure
choice_b: The name of the road running above
choice_c: The posted clearance or height
choice_d: The speed limit posted under the overpass
explanation: After driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After going over a bridge, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_a: The posted weight limit
choice_b: The overall length of the bridge
choice_c: The total number of lanes on the bridge
choice_d: The bridge's construction date
explanation: After going over a bridge, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: If applying for a School Bus endorsement, what must you demonstrate on the road test?
choice_a: A parallel parking maneuver
choice_b: A student discharge
choice_c: An expressway merge only
choice_d: A simulated railroad crossing only
explanation: If you are applying for a School Bus endorsement, you will be required to demonstrate a student discharge.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As you approach a student pick-up point, what warning devices should you activate?
choice_a: Four-way flashers only, with no turn signal
choice_b: The stop arm only, without any lights
choice_c: High-beam headlights
choice_d: Amber warning lights and right turn signals
explanation: As you approach the student pick up, you must activate amber warning lights and right turn signals while decelerating and checking traffic.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: How far away from students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away
choice_b: Exactly 100 feet away
choice_c: At least 50 feet away
choice_d: At least 3 feet away
explanation: The manual requires bringing the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When resuming after a student discharge, what must you do before accelerating away from the stop area?
choice_a: Open all windows for visibility
choice_b: Check all mirrors, turn off warning lights and the stop arm, close the door, and check traffic
choice_c: Immediately accelerate to the posted speed limit
choice_d: Sound the horn twice before moving
explanation: When resuming from the student discharge, you must check all mirrors, turn off warning lights and stop arm, close the door, check traffic, and then accelerate away.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: For manual transmission vehicles, what should you always use to shift?
choice_a: The clutch
choice_b: The horn
choice_c: Only the accelerator pedal
choice_d: The parking brake
explanation: The manual states you should always use the clutch to shift, and double-clutch when shifting an unsynchronized manual transmission.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage

question: What clutch habits should you avoid, according to the manual?
choice_a: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
choice_b: Releasing the clutch smoothly after a shift
choice_c: Using the clutch for every gear change
choice_d: Double-clutching on unsynchronized transmissions
explanation: The manual instructs you not to ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage

question: According to gear usage guidelines, what should you avoid doing while in turns and intersections?
choice_a: Shifting gears
choice_b: Checking your mirrors
choice_c: Braking smoothly
choice_d: Using turn signals
explanation: The manual states, "Do not shift in turns and intersections."
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage

question: What should you select when choosing a gear, according to the gear usage guidelines?
choice_a: A gear that does not rev or lug the engine
choice_b: Any gear regardless of engine strain
choice_c: The lowest gear available at all times
choice_d: The highest gear available at all times
explanation: The manual instructs to select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine, and to avoid grinding or clashing gears.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage

question: How should you apply the brakes, according to the manual's brake usage guidelines?
choice_a: As harshly as possible to stop quickly
choice_b: By pumping the brake pedal rapidly
choice_c: By riding the brake continuously on downgrades
choice_d: Smoothly, using steady pressure, without riding, pumping, or braking harshly
explanation: The manual states: do not ride or pump the brake, do not brake harshly, and brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: Where should you finish a left turn on a multiple lane road?
choice_a: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: In whichever open lane is closest
choice_c: In the left-most lane
choice_d: In the right-most (curb) lane
explanation: The manual specifies the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Unless a lane is blocked, which lane should you move to or remain in?
choice_a: The left-most lane
choice_b: The center turn lane
choice_c: The shoulder of the road
choice_d: The right-most lane
explanation: The manual states, "Move to or remain in right-most lane unless lane is blocked," and to finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: According to the steering guidelines, when should you return both hands to the steering wheel?
choice_a: Once you have completed a gear shift
choice_b: Never, one hand should remain off the wheel while driving
choice_c: Only while making a turn
choice_d: Only after the vehicle comes to a complete stop
explanation: The manual states to keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and to return both hands to the wheel once the shift is complete.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: When should you check mirrors and traffic in relation to an intersection?
choice_a: Only after exiting the intersection
choice_b: Only before entering the intersection
choice_c: Only if a police vehicle is nearby
choice_d: Before, while in, and after the intersection
explanation: The manual instructs to check mirrors and traffic before, while in, and after an intersection.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

question: In which areas should you scan and check traffic especially closely?
choice_a: Only on limited-access expressways
choice_b: Only in parking lots
choice_c: High volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present
choice_d: Only in rural areas with little traffic
explanation: The manual instructs to scan and check traffic in high volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

question: When should turn signals be cancelled, according to the manual?
choice_a: Before beginning the turn or lane change
choice_b: They should never be cancelled manually
choice_c: Only at the very end of the driving test
choice_d: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
explanation: The manual states you must cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change, in addition to using and activating them properly and at appropriate times.
source_note: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals
